Self-contained notes for the course. Each note has the theory with every derivation, the assumptions of the method
with how to check them and what to do when they fail, and code that reproduces every plot and number.
The interactive figures are the same ones used in the [slides](../slides/index.html).

## Machine learning

| # | Note | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 00 | [Supervised learning, splits and CV](machine_learning/00_supervised_learning.html) | problem setup and notation, empirical risk, bias–variance (proof), train/validation/test, K-fold and nested CV, how precise a test metric is, learning curves; assumptions: i.i.d. data, no distribution shift (adversarial validation), grouped and time-ordered data, leakage |
| 01 | [Linear regression](machine_learning/01_linear_regression.html) | loss, gradient, gradient descent and the learning rate, normal equation, convexity, Newton's method, MLE, features and scaling, metrics; OLS statistics (standard errors, intervals, Gauss–Markov); assumptions: linearity, independence, homoscedasticity, normality, collinearity and VIF, exogeneity, leverage and influence |
| 02 | [Logistic regression](machine_learning/02_logistic_regression.html) | sigmoid and odds, cross-entropy = MLE, gradient, convexity, Newton/IRLS, separable data, standard errors and odds ratios, metrics, ROC/AUC, thresholds from costs, calibration; assumptions: linearity in the log-odds, events per variable, influential points; class imbalance |
| 02b | [Generalised linear models](machine_learning/02b_generalized_linear_models.html) | distribution + linear score + link, the exponential family, one gradient and one convexity proof for all GLMs, IRLS, deviance; Poisson regression for claim counts, overdispersion (quasi-Poisson, negative binomial), exposure and offsets, Gamma severity, Tweedie pure premium |
| 03 | [Regularisation, inputs, assumptions](machine_learning/03_regularization_inputs_assumptions.html) | Ridge (SVD view, bias–variance), Lasso (coordinate descent), Elastic Net, MAP view, choosing λ; input variables: scaling, encodings (dummy trap, target encoding), missing values, skewed features, outliers, interactions, pipelines and leakage |
| 04 | [Softmax regression](machine_learning/04_softmax_regression.html) | softmax, identifiability, log-sum-exp, cross-entropy, gradient, convexity, multiclass metrics and confusion matrices; assumptions (IIA, exclusive classes), class imbalance, temperature scaling, one-vs-rest vs softmax |
| 05 | [Support vector classifier](machine_learning/05_support_vector_classifier.html) | margin, Lagrangian, duality and KKT, the dual, SMO, soft margin, kernels and Mercer, hinge loss, sub-gradient descent, multiclass; assumptions and practice: scaling, choosing C and γ, imbalance, Platt probabilities, cost |
| 06 | [Decision trees and CART](machine_learning/06_decision_trees_cart.html) | entropy and Gini, split search, CART from scratch, regression trees, pruning, instability; what trees assume (no extrapolation, axis-aligned splits, greedy search), categorical and missing values, biased feature importance |
| 07 | [Bagging, random forests and boosting](machine_learning/07_bagging_random_forest_boosting.html) | variance of an average, bootstrap and OOB, random forests, feature importance, AdaBoost as exponential-loss minimisation, gradient boosting, XGBoost's second-order derivation, boosting in practice, assumptions |

## Neural networks

| # | Note | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| 00 | [Neural networks and the MLP](neural_networks/00_neural_networks_mlp.html) | neuron = logistic regression, XOR, the MLP, forward pass with numbers, activations and their derivatives, losses as MLE, softmax gradient, universal approximation, non-convexity; practical checks before training |
| 01 | [Backpropagation](neural_networks/01_backpropagation.html) | chain rule on graphs, backpropagation derived and worked with numbers, NumPy code, gradient checking, automatic differentiation, initialisation, vanishing and exploding gradients |
| 02 | [Training: optimisation and regularisation](neural_networks/02_training_optimization_regularization.html) | mini-batches, the learning rate, momentum, RMSProp, Adam, schedules, learning curves, weight decay and AdamW, dropout, BatchNorm (backward pass derived); a debugging guide and the assumptions of training |
| 03 | [CNNs, transfer and multi-task learning](neural_networks/03_cnn_transfer_multitask.html) | convolution and its backward pass, receptive field, pooling, inductive biases, ResNet, transfer and multi-task learning, segmentation (U-Net, Dice), detection (IoU, NMS, AP) |
| 04 | [Embeddings, RNNs and LSTMs](neural_networks/04_rnn_lstm.html) | embeddings, RNN, backpropagation through time, vanishing and exploding gradients, clipping, LSTM and GRU, padding and masking; assumptions of sequence models and look-ahead leakage |
| 05 | [Attention and transformers](neural_networks/05_attention_transformers.html) | attention, √d scaling, multi-head attention, positional encodings (sinusoidal, RoPE), causal mask, cost and KV cache, GPT parameter count, a tiny GPT, decoding, perplexity |
| 06 | [Embeddings, retrieval and RAG](neural_networks/06_embeddings_rag.html) | similarity, TF-IDF, BM25, LSA, neural embeddings, approximate search, retrieval metrics (MRR, nDCG), hybrid retrieval, chunking, RAG and its failure modes |

The hands-on labs are the notebooks in
[`notebooks/`](https://github.com/imagra93/ML-course-labs/tree/main/notebooks), each with an *Open in Colab* button.
